title: Manta surge quickplays (pocket playbook)
body:
Context: quick, personal pocket-runbook for the Manta night/weekend rotations. Not official policy — this is a scratchpad I use when the control plane or inference pools are acting up. Keep things small and actionable; hand this to the next responder in-case of surge.

Quick summary:
- When requests spike and tail-latency climbs >200ms p50 for 2+ minutes, follow the surge play.
- If error-rate >1% sustained for 5m, run the error triage checklist and consider fallback routing.

Goals of this note:
1) Fast triage so customer impact is minimized.
2) Short-term mitigations to keep latency/cost under control.
3) Clear escalation path and post-incident TODOs.

Top-of-shift quick checks (5m):
- Check Alerts dashboard (SRE -> Alerts -> Last 30m) for active throttles, OOMs, model-fallbacks.
- Verify control-plane heartbeats: `curl -sS https://control.redwood.internal/health` (expect 200 + JSON).
- Check Dedicated pool utilization: serving-runtime -> pools -> manta-*/GPU utilization heatmap.
- Slack: skim #oncall and pinned messages for ongoing incidents.

Surge signature patterns (how to spot):
- Latency spike + queued requests + queue-depth rising on a pool (continuous batching limit hit).
- Increased token generation time (per-token CPU/GPU up).
- Error pattern: `KVCache miss` logs followed by client timeouts = backend eviction or model restart.

Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm metrics: p50/p95/p99, QPS, queue_depth for affected model route (time-series).
2) Identify scope: single customer? single region? single model? single pool?
3) If single pool overloaded -> attempt quick scale/evict: serving-runtime -> pool actions -> (scale up + enable-burst if available).
4) If model instance recycling (OOMs) -> mark instance unhealthy and rollback last config (if a recent rollout happened).
5) If control plane errors observed -> switch traffic to alternative region via routing policy (console -> route override -> region fallback).

Short-term mitigations (ordered by safety):
- Enable read-only caching for identical prefix-heavy workloads (toggle in console -> caching advisory -> enable for route).
- Reduce max_tokens or lower max_concurrency on high-cost routes (route-level config).
- Switch to smaller/cheaper compatible model variant for non-critical traffic (fallback mapping: redwood/llama-70b -> redwood/llama-13b-quant).
- Apply temporary rate-limits on noisy api key (console -> tokens -> throttle) for abusive client behaviour.

Common error signatures & immediate actions:
- "kvcache: capacity exceeded" -> Increase KVCache size on pool (if memory available) or evict infrequently-used prefixes. Short-term: reduce batch size.
- "oom: device 0" repeated -> quarantine instance, drain, and restart; if >30% of pool affected, scale up or divert traffic.
- "model-load-failed: out-of-memory" after new rollout -> rollback to previous model version via rollout history (Console -> Rollouts -> revert).
- "rpc: deadline exceeded" -> check inter-service network (platform-engineering slack #network-incidents), retry policy, and client-side timeouts.

Commands & dashboards I use (copy/paste):
- Health: `curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control.redwood.internal/health | jq .`
- Pool list: `rdwctl pools list --region us-west1 --filter manta` (note: rdwctl might be onjump-homebox)
- Node metrics quick: `kubectl top pod -n serving-runtime | grep manta` (if private env)
- Pager summary (copy for escalation): `Manta surge: p95 latency up Xms, QPS Y, error-rate Z% — acting: fallback to 13b + throttling noisy-key`

Escalation matrix (who to ping, in order):
1) On-call SRE (primary): @Ethan Cole (if Pager duty not answered within 5m).
2) Serving runtime lead: @Maya Alvarez (for kernel/compilation issues).
3) Platform infra: @Liu Chen (networking & node provisioning).
4) Product owner for customer-impacting routing decisions: @Samir Joshi.

Template messages (Slack) to copy: 
- Incident start (short): `INCIDENT: Manta surge affecting /v1/generate — p95 +120ms, error-rate 1.8% — triage started. Triage notes: (link to this doc).`
- Customer escalation: `Heads-up: some users may see increased latency on X route. We are actively mitigating by shifting traffic and enabling caching; will update in 15m.`

Temporary runbook: if control plane is degraded
1) Verify control-plane API status. If unreachable, avoid changes in console.
2) Use rdwctl (agent CLI) to adjust routing locally (rdwctl route set-fallback --route <id> --target <model>)
3) Send a rollback message to #oncall and mark change in incident log.
4) If CLI unavailable and control plane down for >10m, escalate to SRE lead and prepare customer-facing status update.

Small hacks & notes I keep forgetting:
- Restarting `model-loader` service in pool sometimes clears stale KV cache objects faster than full node restart. Only do this for controlled nodes.
- When enabling burst capacity, watch costs and set an auto-disable 10m timer (manual reminder in Slack).
- If you reduce concurrency, set back to previous level in congestion-windows step after 30 minutes if stable.

Post-shift handoff template (fill before leaving):
- Current status (OK / Degraded / Incident):
- Actions taken (list):
- Next steps (what to monitor in first 30m):
- Known open items (JIRA / PRs):
- Any shortcuts used (rdwctl commands, console toggles):

Open questions / TODO (personal):
- Add a one-click console button for "divert non-critical traffic" — file a feature request RED-6211.
- Document exact rdwctl flags for model-fallback and add to runbooks.
- Add cost-alert guardrails for burst enable to avoid runaway charges.

Final note: this is intentionally terse — my style for pocket-runbooks. If you inherit this mid-incident, read the top triage checklist and then the Common errors section. Leave a short note in the doc when you sign-off.

Sign-off:
- name: Priya Natarajan
- shift: night (UTC−8)
- started: 2026-02-28 22:00 UTC
